r: Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act requires riders and pillion passengers to wear BIS-standard protective headgear.
p: ₹1,000 and possible disqualification from holding a licence for 3 months (Section 194D).
s: Check the notice for date, place and offence section
Pay or contest within the stated deadline
Wear a BIS-certified helmet and strap it properly
e: Proof of helmet purchase if you were wearing one

r: Section 138(3) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules requires driver and front-seat occupants to wear seat belts.
s: Verify the vehicle number and time on the notice
Pay online or contest if the details are wrong

r: Section 112 sets speed limits; penalties are in Section 183.
p: ₹1,000 for light motor vehicles and ₹2,000 for medium or heavy vehicles. Repeat offences can lead to licence action.
s: Check the recorded speed and the limit on that road
Compare the photo with your vehicle
Pay or contest by the deadline
e: Dashcam footage if you have it

t: Jumping a red light or signal
r: Sections 119 and 177 require obeying traffic signals; dangerous driving falls under Section 184.
p: Commonly ₹500 to ₹5,000 depending on the section applied. Confirm the exact amount on your notice.
s: Read which section is cited
Check the camera image for stop-line position
Pay or contest by the deadline

r: Section 185 prohibits driving with blood alcohol above 30 mg per 100 ml.
p: Up to ₹10,000 and/or 6 months imprisonment; repeat offences up to ₹15,000 and/or 2 years.
s: This is a court matter, so consult a lawyer promptly
Note the testing procedure and any documents given
Attend the court date given

r: Section 3 requires a valid driving licence; Section 181 provides the penalty.
s: If the licence was merely not carried, check whether digital copies (DigiLocker or mParivahan) are accepted
If it expired, renew through Parivahan
If you never held one, apply for a learner’s licence first

r: Section 146 makes at least third-party insurance compulsory.
p: ₹2,000 and/or up to 3 months imprisonment; repeat offences ₹4,000 and/or 3 months (Section 196).
s: Renew the policy immediately
Keep a digital copy on your phone
Contest if the policy was valid at the time

t: Using a mobile phone while driving
r: Using a handheld phone while driving is treated as dangerous driving under Section 184.
p: Up to ₹5,000 for a first offence under current notifications.
s: Check the photo evidence on the notice
Use a mount and hands-free options in future

r: Section 122 prohibits leaving a vehicle in a dangerous position; local authorities set parking rules.
p: Often ₹500 for a first offence (Section 177), plus towing or storage charges set locally.
s: Locate the vehicle using the tow notice
Check signage at the spot
Pay fine and charges, then collect the vehicle with RC and ID

r: Section 190(2) and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules require a valid PUC certificate.
s: Get a fresh PUC test at an authorised centre
Contest if your certificate was valid on the date

r: Section 128 allows only one pillion rider on a motorcycle.
s: Check the notice details
Pay or contest by the deadline

r: E-challans are issued electronically against the vehicle registration number and can be viewed on the Parivahan e-challan portal.
p: Amount depends on the offence cited. Unpaid challans can escalate to a virtual court or affect services.
s: Look up the challan on the official Parivahan e-challan portal
Verify vehicle number, date, place and offence
Pay online, or contest if there is an error
Keep the receipt

r: Section 4 bars driving below the prescribed age; Section 199A makes the guardian or owner liable.
p: ₹25,000 and up to 3 years imprisonment for the guardian or owner; registration may be cancelled for 12 months.
s: Seek legal advice early
Do not allow minors to drive

r: The tenancy agreement and the state’s rent control law govern deposit refunds. Unreasonable withholding can be challenged civilly.
p: No fixed penalty; recovery is by demand, legal notice or a civil suit.
s: Send a written demand citing the agreement
Send a legal notice if ignored
Approach the Rent Controller or a civil court

r: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 lets you complain about defective goods and deficient services to the consumer commissions.
p: Remedies include refund, replacement and compensation; pecuniary limits apply to each commission level.
s: Write to the seller or company and keep the reply
Send a legal notice if unresolved
File online at e-Daakhil

r: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act covers dishonour of a cheque for insufficient funds. A demand notice must be sent within 30 days of the return memo.
p: Imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both.
s: Keep the bank return memo
Send a demand notice within 30 days
If unpaid in 15 days, file a complaint within the following month
